meta.desc: diff — an AI simulator for technical interviews in React, JavaScript, Node.js, and TypeScript. Get your answer reviewed like a pull request.
hero.sub: An AI simulator for technical interviews in React, JavaScript, Node.js, and TypeScript. Pick a topic and level, answer in your own words — and get your answer reviewed line by line, like a pull request.
hero.cardQ: // Q: How does useMemo differ from useCallback?
hero.cardRemoved: useMemo caches the function, and useCallback caches the value.
hero.cardAdded: useMemo caches the value (the result of a computation), while useCallback caches the function itself, so it isn't re-created on every render.
hero.cardComment: A common mix-up. Memo → a value (the memoized value), Callback → the function itself.
how.p: Every interview in diff follows the same route — predictable, like a git flow you already know by heart.
how.1.p: React, JavaScript, Node.js, TypeScript, CSS, SQL — and a level: Junior, Middle, or Senior. Question difficulty adapts to what you pick.
how.2.p: From language basics to architectural decisions, depending on the level. Questions don't repeat from session to session.
how.3.p: In text, with no hints or autocomplete — just like in a real interview.
how.4.p: What's right, what's not, why, and how to phrase it more precisely. Plus a list of topics worth reviewing.
how.5.p: Every attempt is saved. The graph and stats show where you're actually improving — and where you're stuck.
review.h2: A review, not just a grade
review.p: AI doesn't just assign a score. It shows exactly what to phrase differently — the way a senior leaves comments on a pull request.
review.picker.note: Every answer is scored on three criteria: technical accuracy, completeness of explanation, and clarity of phrasing. Then — specific topics to review, not a vague “go study more.”
review.cardQ: // Q: How does the Event Loop handle micro- and macrotasks?
review.cardRemoved: First all the code runs, then all the callbacks run one after another.
review.cardAdded: After the synchronous code, the Event Loop drains the entire microtask queue (Promise, queueMicrotask), and only then takes a single macrotask (setTimeout, I/O).
review.cardComment: The key inaccuracy: all microtasks run at once between each macrotask, not “one by one as they arrive.”
progress.h2: The graph isn't a badge — it's proof
progress.p: Practicing regularly? The graph will show it. The language is specific: how many questions, what accuracy, exactly where the gaps are.
progress.junior: Language and framework basics, common patterns.
hist.p: Every session is its own log entry, like a list of pull requests: topic, level, score, and status.
cta.p: Review your own knowledge today — while there's still time to fix the diff.
